dark_part_of_day.new_value: about 28 to 30 of 48 real minutes (mean over 15 Oct to 2 Dec, lamps on to lamps off, dry overcast)

sources: tools/lane/prototype/project/src/light.js, rules.js (light, weather, seeing, noise, time), clock.js
RULINGS.md 1 Oct, 5 Oct, 7 Oct, 29 Oct, 15 Sep
computed, NOAA solar equations (sunrise, sunset, twilight, sun elevation; Hull 53.7456 N, 0.3367 W; BST to 01:00 UTC on Sun 28 Oct 1990, GMT after)

canon.md (visual target: photoreal, wet, overcast, grimy Britain)
open_points: Place: canon names no region or latitude. The sun times use Hull, 53.74 N (the brief), where LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES used 54.6 N (Tynemouth weather). Hull sunset on 17 Nov is about 16:01 either way within 3 minutes; weather anchors (rain days) are still Tynemouth's. Not canon.
Old 'dusk at 18.25 to night at 19.75' in the prototype (rules.js time) is for a fixed unnamed date and is replaced by the sun-elevation curves here.

Prototype had five weathers (dry, drizzle, rain, heavy, mist). Ruling 5 Oct names three; heavy rain is the 'rain' profile and mist is folded into each profile's mist value. Night mist (prototype) is dropped.
Photocell on 70, off 35 lux is the SC 1000 figure; that 1990 lamps used it is a guess (LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES review).

SOX colour: look file holds linear (1.0, 0.25, 0.0); computed from chromaticity is (1.0, 0.22, 0.0). This file uses the computed value in the warm-up curve's end and lists both. SOX 35 W lumens: 4,770 (modern sheet) vs 4,550 (look note): not used in the game, whose lamp is the game-scaled 167 lm pool.

Real wet hours in a north-east November are probably 15 to 20 percent of hours (judgement, unverified); the weights here give about 18 percent rain and 33 percent drizzle, wetter than climate because the friends' build is a wet-street game by ruling.

Prototype shop-window channel 'early closing' ran 15:30 to 19:30; DEFINITIONS G10 (newer) shuts Quay Street shops at 17:30, so the channel here ends 17:45. Needs the map file's window list to key by door.
Damp floor 0.4 (the street never drier): prototype 0.45; this keeps 'dry overcast' still dark and damp as the 3 and 29 Oct bars need. A fully dry matt road is never shown.
The grade (5.4.3) is written nowhere else: every number in grade is chosen and must be judged in the assembled game against the Hook sheet and KCD2 frames (a rough proof is a finding).

The 4.7 sweep asked for 'sodium warm-up' and 'night visibility radius': both given. Real lux per state is informative only (clear-sky lux above 0 degrees is chosen, not sourced); the game runs on pins and gains.
Clock change is decided (see clock_change); the old open question is closed.
Lamp pool lumens 185 (look file and 4.4 say 167): chosen so pool to fill is at least 10 to 1. The look file's lantern_pool_lumens must change to match, or the finding be logged if it is kept at 167.

location.name: Hull, England
location.clock_rule: local civil time: BST (UTC+1) up to 02:00 BST on 28 Oct 1990, then GMT; the 01:00 to 02:00 hour is played twice

elevation_keys.how_to_use: every curve is keyed by the sun's centre elevation in degrees (computed per minute from date and clock). Interpolate between keys, in log space where 'log' is true, linear otherwise; hold the end values beyond the first and last key. Sunset is elevation -0.833. Values are for dry overcast; weather modifies them through weather.profiles.

exposure_pin.note: day 4.0 and night 0.4 are existing (RULINGS 29 Oct one stop darker, never brightened; look file night_exposure_pin); dusk 0.5 to 1.0 from production/lane/LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES-2026-11-17.md 'What it changes'; the intermediate keys are chosen

sky_intensity.note: 0.70 day and 0.35 night are vignette-pieces overcast_day and wet_night; middle keys chosen

ambient_rgb_linear.note: all chosen: cool grey by day, blue hour at dusk, near neutral dark at night where the night fill (warm) supplies the town-sky glow

fog_rgb_linear.note: chosen: grey by day, warming to the lamp-lit cloud at night

white_balance_K.note: 7000 existing (look file white_temp_day); the rest chosen

night_fill_lux.note: 0.4 existing (look file night_fill_lux, 4 Nov corner note; LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES says about 0.38); ramp chosen

sky_light_gain.note: existing day and night (look file sky_light_gain, sky_light_gain_night)

clear_sky_lux.note: 0, -3, -6, -12 from production/lane/LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES-2026-11-17.md [1]; +5, +10, +20 and -18 chosen (not sourced); informative, and the lamp rule below uses it

fixed_key_light.note: no moving sun (RULINGS 7 Oct) and never sunshine (5 Oct): the sun_intensity 3 of overcast_day is a fixed soft key from one fixed direction, azimuth 200 degrees, elevation 25 degrees (chosen); elevation of the real sun only drives the curves above
fixed_key_light.shadow_note: soft overcast key: a large source angle (30 degrees, chosen) and full shadow softness so shadows are faint and wide and never read as sunshine (5 Oct ruling)

hourly_how_to_read: Three anchor days of rows (whole hours plus extra rows at sunrise and sunset offsets in game minutes) for dry overcast. For any other date interpolate the minute of each curve from elevation_keys using the sun elevation of that minute, or interpolate rows between anchors by date. Time is local civil time. exposure_pin is held across weather (RULINGS 29 Oct: never brightened); weather changes sky_intensity, fog and ambient instead. 'windows_level_dry' multiplies the window channel schedules below.

lamp_rule.photocell_note: old UK cells, SC 1000; 1990 use a guess
lamp_rule.overcast_lux_factor_note: overcast sky is 0.1 to 0.5 of clear (judgement in production/lane/LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES-2026-11-17.md); 0.25, 0.15, 0.08 chosen
lamp_rule.rule: lamps strike on the first minute after solar noon when clear_sky_lux(elevation) * factor falls under 70, and go out the first minute after midnight when it rises over 35. Results are listed per date in days.lamps_on and lamps_off for each weather (dry overcast is 3 to 6 minutes after sunset, rain 7 minutes before).
lamp_rule.warm_up_note: red neon glow first, full yellow in 8 to 15 minutes (production/lane/LIGHT-WEATHER-VALUES-2026-11-17.md [10]); the curve's shape and 12-minute midpoint chosen

lamp.pool_lumens_note: raised from 167 to 185 (chosen) so pool to fill reaches 10 to 1, 5.4.2's 'about ten times'; the fill (0.4 lux) is not touched. 167 gave 9.3 to 1. Real SOX 35 W is about 4,770 lm (modern sheet) or 4,550 (look note); the game lamp is game-scaled.
lamp.bulb_note: reaches 1 m since 28 Oct, adds nothing on the ground
lamp.positions: production/lane/blueprint/data/map.json lamp_columns (93 columns, each 35 W low-pressure sodium, 5.0 m column, lamp 4.83 m); Quay Street has four, about 10 m apart, alternating sides (4.4)

lamp.pool_to_fill_target: at least 10 to 1 under the lamp (judgement, 10 to 25 real)

sim_light.formula: light = clamp(daylight + on * (lamp + always_glow) + late * late_windows + early * early_windows, 0, 1); daylight = 0.07 + 0.93 * (1 - night_factor) where night_factor is 0 by day and 1 below elevation -12 (smoothstep over -0.833 to -12 replaces the prototype's hour smoothstep)

night.window_level_rule: level = 1 - smoothstep(log10 20, log10 300, log10 lux): a window lights from 300 lux (overcast) and is full at 20 lux, so under rain it lights earlier than dry; multiplied by its channel's hour flag

window_colours_linear.note: computed from colour temperature; shop tubes UK White 3500 K, room tungsten 2700 K (judgement)

day_types.how: at 05:00 each game day draw a day type from the period's day_type_weights, seeded by the game seed and the day number; within the day, each spell is drawn from the day type's shares, excluding the current profile; so 'same seed gives the same weather' holds (ER-NIGHT-03)

grip.rule: car grip follows the one wetness value: grip = 1 - 0.31 * wetness (wet braking 1.3 to 1.6 times dry, midpoint 1/1.45 = 0.69 at wetness 1), clamped; the profile grip_factor values are steady-state samples of this

who_is_out.rule: crowd band counts are multiplied by the profile's crowd_factor (dry 1.0, drizzle 0.75, rain 0.5); the same factor halves far voices and activity sounds in sounds.json states; sight_factor multiplies the seeing range; tune:noise.rain_factor multiplies every noise reach (one figure, in tune.json); grip_factor multiplies tyre grip and braking; slipperiness_foot is the chance multiplier for a slip on a sprint or a turn (chosen).
who_is_out.note: the heard-line radius in rain (7 m dry, 6 drizzle, 5 rain) is lines/rules.json and stays there

colour_grade.src: 5.4.3; RULINGS 15 Sep (D28), 21 Sep, 1 Oct; production/reference/README.md; canon.md
mood_words: photoreal, wet, overcast, grimy Britain (canon visual target)
dark, glistening, mirroring sky and buildings (3 Oct bar)
pools of lamp light with darkness between, never one orange wash (1 Oct)
the dull orange glow of an overcast town sky (4 Nov)
colour_grade.mood_to_numbers: cool desaturated grey day; contrast and grain rise toward night; shadows lean cool blue so the sodium pools read as the only warmth; no film warmth added (1990 photographs are warm, which is no colour evidence).
colour_grade.shared_between: browser prototype and Unreal (5.4.3): same numbers; operations in the order above
colour_grade.state_for_elevation: day above sunset, dusk from sunset to -12, night below -12; between states blend by elevation_keys white balance and linear mix of the others over the same range

tonemapper_filmic.note: unverified: Unreal's default filmic values as recalled, not re-read; check against the engine's documentation at build

grain.note: fast stock, the wet overcast one of 1990 film research (DELIVERY.md): grainiest at night; a 'consumer 35 mm' texture, subtle, never a filter look

vignette.light_term: corner darkness = base + 0.25 * (1 - light value at Tom), clamp 0.7: the frame's corners darken with the same light value the watchers use (4.7)

bloom_halation.halation_note: sodium lamps bleed a faint red halo (chosen)

clock_change.rule: the game shows local civil time. At 02:00 BST on Sunday 28 Oct 1990 the clock reads 01:00 GMT again and that hour (01:00 to 02:00) is played twice. Routines keyed to clock time simply hold, so night people stay put. Sun times before 28 Oct are BST, after are GMT (the days table already is).
